record.paper_title: Hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin methods for second-order elliptic problems: overview, a new result and open problems
record.original_question: Develop a systematic procedure that transforms stabilizations into spaces, reversing the direction of Theorem 5.1, so that any HDG method can be rewritten as a mixed method in a mathematically useful way that exposes genuinely new approximation spaces and may even produce a discontinuous Galerkin method for pure convection with no stabilization function.

evidence.quote: Transforming stabilizations into spaces. Let us elaborate this last idea a little further. Theorem 5.1 shows how to transform spaces into stabilizations, but it seems possible to transform stabilizations into spaces too. As a consequence, we could then rewrite any HDG method as a mixed method. Of course, we do not want just to change the way of presenting the original HDG scheme. So, we could look for the possibility of using new spaces which would render the scheme better. In particular, this would mean that we could have a DG method for pure convection problems without stabilization function.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and setting. Consider second-order elliptic (and convection–diffusion) boundary value problems on a polygonal/polyhedral domain Ω ⊂ R^d discretized on a conforming simplicial (or polytopal) mesh T_h with skeleton ∂T_h = ⋃_{K∈T_h} ∂K. A hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin (HDG) method seeks an approximation (q_h, u_h, û_h) ∈ V_h × W_h × M_h to (∇u, u, u|_{∂T_h}) by imposing, for every K ∈ T_h,
   (q_h, v)_K − (u_h, ∇·v)_K + ⟨û_h, v·n⟩_{∂K} = 0,    ∀v ∈ V_h(K),
   −(q_h, ∇w)_K + ⟨q̂_h·n, w⟩_{∂K} = (f, w)_K,           ∀w ∈ W_h(K),
where the numerical trace of the flux is defined by
   q̂_h · n = q_h · n + τ (u_h − û_h) on ∂K,
for a prescribed (typically piecewise constant) stabilization function τ ≥ 0, together with single-valuedness ⟦q̂_h·n⟧ = 0 on interior faces and a boundary condition on û_h.

A mixed method, by contrast, replaces the stabilization mechanism by a careful choice of the local spaces V_h(K), W_h(K) (for example Raviart–Thomas, Brezzi–Douglas–Marini, or M-decomposition based spaces) so that the corresponding scheme is well-posed and convergent without any stabilization parameter τ. A known result (referred to here as the "spaces-to-stabilizations" theorem) shows how, given suitable enriched local spaces, one can eliminate them in favour of an equivalent HDG-type stabilization τ acting on smaller polynomial spaces.

Problem. Develop a systematic, mathematically rigorous procedure that performs the converse transformation: given an arbitrary HDG method specified by local polynomial spaces V_h(K), W_h(K), M_h(F) and a stabilization function τ, construct enriched local spaces Ṽ_h(K), W̃_h(K) (and trace space M̃_h(F)) such that

  (i) the HDG method based on (V_h, W_h, M_h, τ) is equivalent to a mixed method based on (Ṽ_h, W̃_h, M̃_h) with no stabilization (τ ≡ 0);

  (ii) the construction is constructive and algorithmic, applying to every HDG method (in particular for arbitrary polynomial degree k and on simplicial/polytopal meshes in any dimension d ≥ 2);

  (iii) the resulting enriched spaces are genuinely new (not merely a tautological reformulation of the original scheme) and improve some quantifiable property of the discretization, such as approximation order, superconvergence, conservation, or computational cost;

  (iv) as a particular consequence, the procedure yields a discontinuous Galerkin discretization for the pure convection problem β·∇u = f (with prescribed inflow data) that is well-posed and convergent without any stabilization function.

Provide either such a procedure together with proofs of well-posedness, equivalence, and convergence, or a proof that no such universal transformation exists.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an explicitly open research direction in the HDG literature, calling for a converse to the known "spaces-to-stabilizations" construction. No published systematic procedure realizing this converse in full generality (and producing a stabilization-free DG method for pure convection) appears to be available; the question seems to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin methods for second-order elliptic problems: overview, a new result and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Lists open problems for HDG methods, including transforming stabilizations into spaces and producing DG methods for pure convection without stabilization.
status_evidence.claim: The transformation of stabilizations into spaces is identified as an open problem in the HDG literature.
